Subject: GPU pool throughput guarantees and pricing — benchmark packet and next steps

Hi Jill / Acme team —

Thanks again for the call last week. We ran the dedicated-pool benchmark you asked for (model: opensource-xxl-v1, 512-token prompt, sampling top-p) against the configuration we discussed: 4 x A100-equivalent cards in a single reserved GPU pool with continuous batching enabled. The short summary is below and the full artifacts are attached.

Summary (observed):
- Aggregate steady-state throughput (inferred request/sec at 8 concurrent streams): 480 req/s per 4-GPU pool
- Per-GPU throughput: ~120 req/s
- Latency (median/p95): 210 ms / 420 ms (token generation measured; end-to-end request latency includes ~30–60 ms network overhead)
- KV/prefix cache hit uplift: +18% effective throughput when warm
- Observed tail variance during burst tests (200% traffic spike): p99 jumps to ~1.1s but overall queueing recovered within 30s with autoscaling policy applied.

What this implies for your SLOs: to guarantee 2,000 req/s steady throughput with p95 < 500 ms, we recommend reserving 5 x 4-GPU pools (20 GPUs) with conservative headroom for burst (or 4 pools + burst capacity). That map corresponds to the commit tiers we sketched in the pricing grid attached.

Requested decisions / asks:
1) Which commit horizon are you leaning toward? (6/12/24 months) — affects discount banding.
2) Can you confirm the target steady-state TPS and acceptable p95 latency for the SLA? We used 2,000 req/s / p95 500 ms as a working assumption.
3) Any procurement constraints (billing cadence, PO lead times) we should fold into the contract?

Attachments: acme-20260803-bench-summary.csv (results), tps-traces-20260802.zip (perf traces), dedicated-pricing-grid-v2.pdf (pricing bands / discount table).

Next steps: Marcus will draft the pricing band with a sample reserved-commit seat schedule; Laura will prepare an exec one-pager for the commercial terms. If you want, we can also schedule a live walkthrough of the perf dashboard this week.

Thanks —

Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

--

Hi Stephanie —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed numbers. A couple of clarifying Qs before we commit: 

1) The 480 req/s per 4-GPU pool number — is that with continuous batching and KV cache warm? If cache cold, what does steady throughput look like?
2) Our production mix has 70% short prompts (~64 tokens) and 30% long prompts (~1,024 tokens) — how much variability should we expect vs your single-profile run?
3) On the discount bands: can you give a concrete monthly $/GPU equivalent so we can plug into our TCO model?

Also need to share the procurement constraints: Acme requires 60 days to issue PO for new vendors and prefers annual billing for committed capacity.

If it's helpful, we can jump on a 30-minute session with your engineering team tomorrow.

— Jill
Jill Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI

Jill / team —

Quick answers:
1) 480 req/s per 4-GPU pool is the warm-cache, continuous-batching figure. Cold-cache runs (no prefix caching + cold KV) measured ~360 req/s per 4-GPU pool under identical concurrency. We include cache-warm assumptions in the SLA definition; if you need strict cold-cache guarantees we can size differently or adjust the SLA pricing.

2) Mixed workload: with your 70/30 short/long split we expect effective throughput to sit between the short- and long-run numbers; ballpark for the mix is ~520 req/s per 4-GPU pool (short prompts increase token-generation parallelism). We'll run a synthetic mixed-profile test if you want formal numbers.

3) Pricing: attached is the updated pricing grid. Representative examples (monthly committed pricing per GPU-equivalent, list price, US region):
- 6-mo commit, 20-GPU effective commit: $14,000 / GPU / month (list) — we can offer a 12% off list for an initial 6-month term if signed this quarter.
- 12-mo commit, 20-GPU: $13,000 / GPU / month — 20% off list
- 24-mo commit, 20-GPU: $12,000 / GPU / month — 28% off list

These numbers include reserved capacity SLA (throughput guarantee with 5% credit on missed SLOs) and standard support. Higher-tier SLAs (faster incident response, financial credits) available for an additional fee.

Operational notes: we propose a phased rollout — start with 2 pools (8 GPUs) in month 1 for canary traffic, validate with your telemetry for 3 weeks, then ramp to full committed pools. We'll provide a runbook for traffic shaping and fallback to hosted models if needed.

If the 60-day PO cadence is real, we'll slot the start date accordingly and include a clause for a pro-rated first month.

Next action: Stephanie, can you confirm whether Acme wants the mixed-profile run before finalizing the commit tier? If they approve the 12-mo band, I will provision the discount grid and a draft term sheet.

—Marcus

Jill —

Thanks — we can run the mixed-profile test this afternoon (ETA for artifacts: 24 hours). On SLA credits: we measure per-pool hourly windows against committed throughput and p95 latency. If a window misses the committed throughput or exceeds p95, we aggregate the shortfall minutes over the billing period and credit at the per-minute fraction of the monthly committed amount (example calculation included in the attached one-pager). There is a 30% cap on aggregate credits per billing month to limit blowouts.

We can hold the quoted discount schedule for 45 days. Action items for clarity:
- Marcus: run mixed-profile test (70/30) and upload csv + traces + dashboard link to the deal.
- Stephanie: prepare a short commercial term sheet with the 12-mo pricing and the pro-rated start date option for Acme procurement.
- Jill / Acme: confirm whether you want the additional faster incident SLA (we'll price separately).

I'll attach the SLA-credit worked example and the proposed deployment timeline.

Laura Bennett
